title: Shape read
description: A SHAPE is the constraint set a geometry is a solution to — not the geometry, not the picture, not the name the field gave it. See SHAPE_SPEC.md, which is upstream of this file and is not restated here. A record carrying solving_for, constraints, why_not_the_other_geometry and a removal_test is a shape entry. A record missing the removal test is a geometry note, and is marked as one rather than rejected. METHOD_SPEC.md states the epistemic class of that spec and is read first: constraint-set reasoning is a METHOD, not a claim, and a method is not falsifiable and does not need to be. The falsifiable layer is the individual read, which is why removal_test is required here.

geometry.description: What is visible of the shape. The readout, not the object — and the QUESTION, not the answer. May be empty only on a shadow read, where the geometry is not visible and the shape is described by the gaps it casts instead.

solving_for.description: Read order step 1. What is being distributed, moved, balanced or held. State the quantity.

constraints.description: Read order step 2. What bounds the solution. Include the external and heterogeneous ones — substrate the system did not choose — not only the ones internal to the flow rule.

sits.description: internal_uniform: boundary known in advance, same everywhere — the geometry is a solution to a stated problem. external_heterogeneous: the boundary is whatever substrate was hit — the geometry is a record of the substrate, and must not be read as an optimum.

ratio.description: State constraints as ratios, not lengths. Lengths are outputs; ratios set the form.

why_not_the_other_geometry.description: Read order step 3, and the instrument. Steps 1 and 2 can be done wrong and still look finished; this one fails loudly.

removal_test.description: Which constraint, if REMOVED, changes the geometry — plus a case where it is genuinely absent. If the form is unchanged the constraint was not load-bearing and the read is wrong. A failed test is a measurement, not an embarrassment: it locates a constraint that differs between the two cases.

scale_index.description: Every physical instance has a characteristic scale; below and above it the same mechanism reads as noise. Locating it is part of the read.

across_levels.description: invariant: one mechanism. drifts: family resemblance, and the read is weaker than it looks. Not yet measured for any shape in this ecosystem.

independent_recurrence.description: Different substrates, different materials, no shared ancestry, same geometry. Separate runs converging is what carries the weight — a fitted exponent is a label on it, and the fit describes the surviving sample.

read_path.description: direct: the geometry is visible and the read order applies. shadow: it is not — often because the constraint that would make it visible is the one nobody is measuring — so the shape is described by the gaps it casts.

tangents.description: Shadow reads only. Each statement is one gap; the object is what they are all tangent to. They will look scattered and may appear to conflict — they are separate tangents to one boundary, not competing claims, and a linear reading discards half the outline.

outline_state.description: Shadow reads only. The read is complete when the gaps constrain the object to one form. Until then it is under-outlined, which is a stated state and not a failure.

confidence.description: A separate readout from the pattern. A read at 0.4 is not a claim held at 0.4 — it is an uncoalesced marker with a stated gradient, and is not to be resolved in either direction on its behalf.

basis.description: What moved it. RECURRENCE_COUNT is deliberately absent and is rejected at validation: a read is NOT upgraded by more instances sharing the geometry without a checked constraint set.

disappearances.description: A shape appearing tells you the constraints were met. A shape disappearing tells you at least one was removed, but not which — informative and underdetermined. A timestamped intervention bounds the candidate set; that is the handle. Reporting a disappearance as a failed pattern reports the wrong finding: it is the constraint set being changed.

sample_frame.description: If a domain is removed from the frame, the recurrence check cannot run there by construction and returns a null that reads as absence. An excluded domain is UNTESTED, not inapplicable.
